subject: Evidence request: operational proof for no-training / subprocessor gating
messages:
From: Lara O'Neill <lara.oneill@medforge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: MedForge Legal <legal@medforge.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operational evidence for no-training and subprocessor gating

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Before we can move the DPA forward internally, Legal and InfoSec need an operational evidence pack to validate two items: 1) your "no-training / model-improvement opt-out" commitment and 2) the gating for downstream subprocessors that access tenant interaction data.

Specifically MedForge needs:
- A written statement describing how Redwood prevents customer data from being used to improve models (including both host-hosted and dedicated/private modes).
- A current subprocessor inventory (names, country, function, and whether they see raw prompts/responses).
- A diagram and short narrative of the runtime dataflow when a user message is processed (ephemeral/session keys, KV cache behavior, any persistence endpoints).
- KMS residency details (where customer keys may be stored/used; onshore/offshore options).
- Confirmation whether ephemeral chat sessions (session-scoped keys) are covered by the no-train commitment and whether outputs (generated text) are treated as customer-owned IP.

Can you provide the above by end of next week? If you have a standard evidence pack or an Ops playbook URL, that would speed review.

Appreciate it — we want to keep the procurement timeline tight, but InfoSec will escalate if we can't validate these controls.

Best,
Lara
Senior Counsel, MedForge Therapeutics

--
Attachments: none

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lara O'Neill <lara.oneill@medforge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for no-training and subprocessor gating

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in David (Privacy/Compliance) and Markus (Security Ops) to assemble the pack.

High level answers up front:
- No-training commitment: Redwood offers a contractual no-training ("no model improvement") option per-tenant. For hosted customers this is an opt-out flag tied to the tenant; for Dedicated/Private deployments the default is no shared-model updates unless the customer consents. We will provide the exact contractual language you can include in the DPA.
- Ephemeral sessions: session-scoped interactions are covered by the same opt-out when the tenant has chosen it; ephemeral KV cache is not persisted beyond the session when the opt-out is enabled.
- Outputs/IP: Redwood's standard position is that customers retain ownership of their prompt/response content. We can provide the clause and examples in the DPA redline.

Planned deliverables and timeline:
1) Subprocessor inventory + function mapping (CSV) — David will attach.
2) Dataflow diagram + short runbook describing how prompts are routed, when caching occurs, and what is persisted — Markus will attach.
3) KMS residency options + certificate references — we'll summarize and include the KMS regions.
4) Example DPA language & a single-page narrative describing the operational proof steps InfoSec can follow to validate controls.

We should be able to send the complete evidence pack and a DPA redline by EOD Tuesday (2027-03-23). If you need faster escalation, let me know and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: (planned) subprocessor_inventory_20270321.csv, dataflow_diagram_v2.png

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lara O'Neill <lara.oneill@medforge.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for no-training and subprocessor gating

Lara / Neha — attaching the subprocessor inventory and the dataflow diagram for your review. Quick notes below so InfoSec has context when they look through: 

- subprocessor_inventory_20270321.csv: includes name, primary country, role (e.g., metrics ingestion, SFTP export, third-party logging), whether they have access to raw prompts/responses (yes/no), and the contractual gating we enforce (SCOR/attestation cadence).
- dataflow_diagram_v2.png: shows request path from customer agent -> routing layer -> serving runtime -> KV cache -> tokenization -> output; includes the two persistence lanes (ephemeral session cache and optional SFTP export) and where KMS-wrapped keys are used.

Operational proof steps (short):
1) Validate tenant flag: InfoSec can confirm the tenant's "no-train" flag in our control plane audit logs (we can provide a sampling of audit entries).
2) Inspect runtime: we can provide a timeboxed runbook execution where an engineer demonstrates a request flow and shows that no artifacts are written to model training buckets when the flag is set.
3) KMS verification: we will provide key ARNs/IDs and the region mapping; for onshore KMS requirement we can scope keys to the customer's chosen region in Dedicated/Private deployment.

I'll attach the CSV and PNG as stubs here (see attachments). Happy to hop on a 30-min session with your InfoSec to walk through the runbook.

-David
Director, Privacy & Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20270321.csv, dataflow_diagram_v2.png

From: Lara O'Neill <lara.oneill@medforge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: MedForge Legal <legal@medforge.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for no-training and subprocessor gating

Thank you — this is helpful and aligns with what InfoSec asked for. A couple of follow-ups after a quick skim: 

- Could you confirm whether third-party telemetry/metrics vendors (listed in CSV) receive unredacted prompt text? We prefer vendors to only receive telemetry hashes or aggregated metrics unless explicitly scoped in the DPA.
- DPA redline: we've attached a short set of suggested edits and one proposed language tweak to the ownership clause (see attachment). Please confirm if the "outputs are customer-owned" phrasing can be tightened to explicitly exclude Redwood derivative models or product analytics usage.
- Ephemeral sessions: good to know they're covered by the flag. Please add one sentence to the runbook that explicitly demonstrates session-scoped KV eviction and the absence of training-bucket writes during the demo run.

If you can incorporate those changes into the pack and share a final zip by EOD Tuesday, we'll route this to procurement. If it's easier to run the demo with InfoSec live, the team is available Wednesday AM.

Best,
Lara
Senior Counsel, MedForge Therapeutics

--
